_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. status: active = connector-only, a reprint would clobber it; upstreamed = also fixed in the press, a reprint from a fixed press regenerates it, but the back-port must still be present today.

handfixes.summary: `SaveTokens` no longer clears the ClientID and ClientSecret env-override markers, so an env-supplied client secret is never written to the credentials file
handfixes.why: PR #268 established that a credential supplied through the environment is never persisted. It is enforced by two guards that both read Config.envOverrides: configForSave() substitutes the file's value for any env-marked field, and updateFileConfigField() returns early for one. SaveTokens deleted the ClientID and ClientSecret markers before calling either, which defeated both, so `auth login` wrote the operator's long-lived client secret into credentials.toml. Observed live against a real ImmyBot tenant: with IMMYBOT_CLIENT_SECRET set only as a session variable and no --save flag passed, credentials.toml came back containing client_secret in plaintext, while `doctor` still reported credentials_location as env:IMMYBOT_CLIENT_SECRET. That mismatch is the whole danger: an operator who deliberately keeps secrets in session-scoped variables is told the secret is not on disk while a copy of it is. The minted access token, refresh token, and expiry keep their markers cleared, because those values originate in SaveTokens and login is exactly when they should be written. ClearCredentials (logout) also keeps clearing all five deliberately: it zeroes the fields and must overwrite whatever is already on disk, so an early return there would strand the secret. 61 of the 66 skills in this repo emit the same SaveTokens body, so this is an engine-level defect and not an ImmyBot quirk.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Fix in the press template so SaveTokens preserves env-override markers for the credential inputs (ClientID, ClientSecret) while still persisting the minted trio. Until then every reprint reintroduces the leak, and the same fix is owed to the other 60 connectors that emit this body.

asserts.contains: ClientID and ClientSecret deliberately keep their env-override markers

handfixes.summary: the client-credentials scope is derived from the ImmyBot instance URL instead of the generator's `api://{client_id}/.default` default
handfixes.why: ImmyBot's Entra application publishes the tenant's own instance URL as its App ID URI, so the correct client-credentials scope is https://<subdomain>.immy.bot/.default. ImmyBot's published API reference builds exactly that value (scope=$ApiEndpointUri/.default where $ApiEndpointUri is the instance base URL), confirmed against their documentation. The generator's default for any Microsoft Entra token URL is api://{client_id}/.default, which names the caller's own app registration as the resource rather than ImmyBot, and is therefore always wrong here. applyDerivedOAuthScope populates IMMYBOT_OAUTH_SCOPE before any token mint, which is the durable seam because the generated resolveClientCredentialsScope reads that variable first. Verified live: with the derivation in place, `auth login` mints a token against a real tenant and `sync` returns 119,654 records.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Teach the press to read a server-URL-derived audience for Entra client-credentials flows so instance-scoped App ID URIs do not need a per-connector hand-fix.

handfixes.summary: the `computers` resource requests pageSize=1000 instead of the spec default 25, because GET /api/v1/computers is a capped-limit endpoint with no way to fetch a second page
handfixes.why: GET /api/v1/computers declares exactly four query parameters (name, tenantId, orderByUpdatedDate, pageSize), confirmed by reading a live instance's swagger.json. There is no cursor, page, skip or offset, so the empty cursorParam is correct and no pagination fix is possible: probing page=1, page=2, Page=2 and skip=5 against a real tenant returned byte-identical result sets every time. pageSize is a ceiling on a single response, and the profiler mistook its spec default of 25 for a page size. The consequence was a silent cap rather than an error: a tenant holding 57 computers mirrored 25 of them and sync reported success. `computers` is the resource the offline commands join on most (149 references across internal/cli), so every command answered from 44% of the fleet while presenting a complete-looking result. Verified live before and after: pageSize=25 returns 25 rows, pageSize=100 returns 57, pageSize=1000 returns 57; after the change `sync --resources computers` stores 57 and, because a short page proves completeness, last_synced_at advances to a real timestamp instead of the zero value it had been stuck on. Raising the ceiling is the only lever the endpoint offers, so the existing full-page warning stays the truncation signal for an instance larger than the ceiling, and computers-paged (real skip/take pagination) is the alternative source for those.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Teach the profiler to distinguish a response-size ceiling from a page size when an endpoint declares a limit parameter but no cursor, page, skip or offset parameter. Emitting the spec default as the page size silently truncates every such resource.

handfixes.summary: three parameter-required lookup endpoints are removed from defaultSyncResources, because sync cannot supply their required query parameter and they answer HTTP 400 on every run
handfixes.why: The profiler wired /api/v1/chocolatey/find-packages-by-id, /api/v1/maintenance-actions/maintenance-item and /api/v1/maintenance-actions/version into the default sync walk as if they were list endpoints. None of them is: each requires a query parameter (packageId, maintenanceItem, version respectively) that a bulk sync has no value for, so all three answered HTTP 400 'The <field> field is required.' on every run. This is the same class of defect as the ThreatLocker sync fixed in PR #222, where the profiler wired sync to GET dropdown helpers that were never bulk-list surfaces. The three names stay in knownSyncResourceNames and syncResourcePath so an explicit --resources selection still resolves and no other code path breaks; only the default walk drops them. Verified live: sync errored=3 before, errored=0 after, with resource count 68 -> 65 and no loss of records.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Teach the profiler to keep endpoints with required query parameters out of the generated sync surface. An endpoint that cannot be called without a caller-supplied value is not a list endpoint.

asserts.contains: are deliberately absent, for the same

handfixes.summary: doctor reports the instance subdomain as its own check and stops pointing at a nonexistent `auth setup` subcommand
handfixes.why: Two separate inaccuracies in the same output. First, env_vars counts only the OAuth trio and prints 'OK 3/3 available', while the auth_instructions in the same payload tell the operator to set four variables. The one it omitted, IMMYBOT_SUBDOMAIN, is the one whose absence fails worst: without it applyDerivedOAuthScope cannot build https://<subdomain>.immy.bot/.default, the scope silently falls back to the generated api://{client_id}/.default, which names the caller's own app registration rather than ImmyBot, and the operator gets an opaque Entra rejection or a 401 rather than being told which variable is missing. A dedicated instance check now names it. Second, auth_hint told operators to run 'immybot-cli auth setup', which does not exist; the real subcommands are login, logout, set-token and status, so the hint sent people to a dead command at the exact moment they were stuck. Note this bad hint is not ImmyBot-specific: five skills in this repo emit it while defining no such command (appdirect, crowdstrike, halopsa, immybot, ninjaone), and halopsa and ninjaone are shipped connectors.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: In the press: emit the auth hint from the set of subcommands the connector actually generates rather than a fixed string, and include every required template variable in the doctor env-var check rather than only the auth credentials. Also worth a repo-wide sweep for the four other skills already emitting the dead `auth setup` hint.

handfixes.summary: the zero last_synced_at is treated as "never completed a pass" rather than a timestamp, so staleness stops reporting a 292-year age against fresh data
handfixes.why: A resource that has never completed a full sync pass stores the zero time rather than NULL: SaveSyncProgress writes a parseable zero so GetSyncState can scan without a NULL conversion error, and the watermark only advances when sync can prove it saw the whole result set (a page-capped or truncated run correctly withholds it). That makes the zero a sentinel, not a timestamp. Two places read it as one. sync_hint filtered with `last_synced_at IS NOT NULL`, which does not exclude a non-NULL zero, so ORDER BY last_synced_at ASC LIMIT 1 selected the sentinel as the oldest row every time; doctor gated on lastSynced.Valid, which is likewise true for a zero. time.Since(zero) then saturates time.Duration at its 292-year maximum, so every offline command printed 'local store data is 2562047h47m0s old' against data written seconds earlier and doctor reported status stale with oldest_age 2562047h47m0s on a mirror that had just synced. Measured live on a 64-resource store: before, oldest_age 2562047h47m0s; after, oldest_age 50m0s with never_synced 40 reported separately. doctor now also separates the two reasons a store is not fresh, because 'older than stale_after' and 'never completed a pass' need different actions, and the hint distinguishes an empty store from one holding partial data from a truncated run.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: In the press: give the never-completed state its own representation rather than overloading the zero time, or make every reader treat a zero watermark as a distinct state. Any connector whose API returns full pages without a usable cursor hits this, so the failure is not ImmyBot-specific.

handfixes.summary: the runtime error paths and the MCP tool errors stop pointing at a nonexistent `auth setup` subcommand (doctor.go was fixed first; these 7 sites were missed)
handfixes.why: `auth setup` does not exist in this CLI - the real subcommands are login, logout, set-token and status. The doctor hint was corrected under `doctor-reports-instance-and-a-real-auth-command`, but the same dead string was emitted from seven other places that fire on the exact failures a new operator hits: helpers.go's HTTP 400-auth, 401, 403 and HTML-instead-of-JSON branches, and three auth branches in the MCP tool layer. Cobra answers an unrecognised subcommand by printing help and exiting 0, so an operator who followed the hint saw a help screen, got exit 0, re-ran doctor and was still 'not configured' - nothing signalled that the advice itself was wrong, and these are agent-first CLIs where exit 0 reads as success. All seven now point at `auth login` (with `auth status` as the inspection command). Fixing one surface and missing its twin is exactly the failure this ledger exists to prevent.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press fix as the doctor entry, applied to EVERY auth-hint emission site rather than only the doctor payload: generate the hint from the connector's real auth subcommand set. A template that hardcodes `auth setup` is wrong for any connector that does not generate it.

handfixes.summary: agent-context AND the MCP context tool both list IMMYBOT_SUBDOMAIN alongside the OAuth trio, so an agent reading runtime truth on either surface sees all four required inputs
handfixes.why: AGENTS.md instructs agents to start from `immybot-cli agent-context --pretty` as 'current runtime truth', but its auth.env_vars carried only IMMYBOT_TENANT_ID, IMMYBOT_CLIENT_ID and IMMYBOT_CLIENT_SECRET. IMMYBOT_SUBDOMAIN is the one whose absence fails worst: it derives the OAuth scope https://<subdomain>.immy.bot/.default, and without it the scope falls back to api://{client_id}/.default, naming the caller's own app registration rather than ImmyBot, so Entra rejects the token opaquely. This is the same 3-of-4 undercount already fixed in doctor under `doctor-reports-instance-and-a-real-auth-command`; agent-context is its twin and was missed. The CLIENT_SECRET description also said 'Set during initial auth setup', naming the nonexistent `auth setup` command. ROUND-2 ADDENDUM: the first pass fixed cli/agent_context.go only and missed its MCP twin, internal/mcp/tools.go handleContext - which is the surface most agents actually read, and whose own comment claims the two 'cannot drift'. They had drifted: env_vars listed 3 while the instructions field in the same payload named 4. Both surfaces are now asserted below, because asserting only one is what allowed the drift. ROUND-4 ADDENDUM: `auth status` and `auth login --help` still declared only CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET. Following that hint literally produced 'Logged in.' exit 0 with the scope falling back to api://<client-id>/.default - the silent wrong-scope failure this ledger describes, on the one surface a human actually reads when they are not yet authenticated. auth.go now names all four.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: In the press: build the agent-context auth env-var list from the same source as the doctor env-var check, so a connector cannot declare a different required set in two places. Any template variable required to construct the token request belongs in both.

handfixes.summary: cobratree/classify.go honours the `pp:parent-group` annotation, so parent command groups do not each ship as a no-op MCP tool (44 tools instead of 121)
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.3 fixed the default-deny MCP gate but reintroduced ~77 no-op parent-group tools: every intermediate command group was emitted as its own callable tool that does nothing but print help. Measured on this connector: 44 tools with the annotation handling, 121 without. A 121-tool server buries the 44 real ones and burns the agent's tool budget. This handling exists in 0 of the 63 shipped connectors, so it is NOT something a reprint will regenerate - a reprint against a press without the equivalent fix silently reinstates all 77. Recorded here because the edit arrived inside the bulk vendoring commit, which check_handfixes.py --changed exempts as a reprint, so CI would not otherwise have caught its loss.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: In the press: suppress parent-group commands from the MCP tool surface at generation time rather than requiring a per-connector annotation handler. Track against the 4.30.3 no-op-tool regression.

handfixes.summary: platform/migration.go passes the backup destination to `VACUUM INTO` as a bound parameter instead of interpolating a hand-quoted path
handfixes.why: SQLite takes VACUUM INTO's destination as an expression, so the generated code built it by string-quoting the target path. A path containing a single quote (or any crafted sequence) breaks out of that quoting and is executed as SQL, on a path that can come from --db / IMMYBOT_HOME / the data dir. Binding the value removes the injection surface entirely. Present in 0 of 63 shipped connectors, so a reprint reverts it silently, and no test exercises this path - the assert below is the only thing standing between a reprint and the reintroduced defect.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: In the press: emit `VACUUM INTO ?` with a bound argument in the migration template. Worth a fleet sweep - every shipped connector still interpolates the path.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For immybot the manifest gained: IMMYBOT_BASE_URL, IMMYBOT_TOKEN_URL, IMMYBOT_USER_AGENT, PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE. server.json gained: IMMYBOT_BASE_URL, IMMYBOT_TOKEN_URL, IMMYBOT_USER_AGENT, PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: IMMYBOT_BASE_URL, IMMYBOT_TOKEN_URL, IMMYBOT_USER_AGENT, PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: cli/NOTICE names this connector's contributor, in the Apache-2.0 attribution channel
handfixes.why: CONTRIBUTING.md and the public contributing page promise that a contributor's credit survives a regeneration. Nothing enforced that. The press regenerates cli/NOTICE from its own template, which carries the CLI Printing Press attribution but not this repo's per-connector 'contributed by' sentence, so a reprint would silently delete the only place the credit lives. PR #283 moved contributor credit out of per-file copyright headers and into NOTICE, which makes this line the load-bearing copy rather than a duplicate. Pinning the exact sentence here is what turns the promise into a checked one.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: The press has no per-connector contributor field, so there is nothing to encode upstream today. If one is added, the NOTICE template should emit this sentence by construction. Related: the press stamps the copyright header from whoever ran the generator, filed as mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4326 closed 2026-08-25 as not planned (wontfix: operator-stamped attribution is product/config work), no fix landed; this hand-fix is permanent unless re-filed; do NOT cite #4326 as open.

asserts.contains: The ImmyBot connector was contributed by Abhi Saini (@geekbrownbear).

handfixes.summary: IMMYBOT_NO_CONFIG_WRITE makes every credential write a no-op (token cache included) while leaving the `auth logout` erase working, and the MCP server honours it too (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270, raised by @Xenith-B off the back of #266. #266 stopped env-supplied client credentials reaching disk; the MINTED access token still landed in ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext and there was no supported way to turn that off. Their workaround was `--config NUL`, which is OS-specific, undocumented, makes doctor report a false 'not configured', and - the part that matters most - does not cover the MCP servers at all, because internal/mcp resolved its own hardcoded config path and ignored --config. Three deliberate boundaries make this switch honest rather than merely quiet. (1) ClearTokens keeps calling save() directly: it is the ERASE path, and routing it through the guard would make `auth logout` silently inert, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (2) `auth login` and `auth set-token` REFUSE and name the variable rather than reporting a save that did not happen - a false success is the same defect class as a doctor that says credentials are fine without checking. (3) newMCPClient already resolved through config.Load(""), the resolver the CLI uses, on this connector, so the MCP server honours both IMMYBOT_CONFIG and this switch with no edit needed here; that is the half the issue says is uncovered today, and the tools.go assert below pins the resolver so a reprint cannot quietly hardcode a path again. The variable is declared on all three install channels because for a Claude Desktop install the manifest prompt is the ONLY channel that can set an environment variable. Class C, new documented surface. GENERATOR-class: a reprint drops the switch entirely and silently restores the plaintext token cache.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit <PREFIX>_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (or an equivalent) as part of the standard config surface, with the same three boundaries: the erase path exempt, explicit save commands failing loudly rather than no-oping, and the MCP server resolving its config through config.Load("") instead of a hardcoded home-relative path. The hardcoded path in internal/mcp/tools.go is a generator defect in its own right - it makes --config and <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

asserts.contains: | `auth login` / `auth set-token` | Refuse, naming the variable, instead of reporting a save that did not happen. |

handfixes.summary: `recall` and `playbook list` are annotated mcp:local-write, not mcp:read-only, because both open the writable learn store and record a row (issue #275 finding 4)
handfixes.why: issue #275 finding 4. `recall` (teach.go) declared mcp:read-only=true, opened the WRITABLE store via store.OpenWithContext and inserted a learn event on every call; `playbook list` (teach_playbook.go) was marked read-only and appended an audit record. The annotation is what an MCP host reads to decide what to auto-approve, so a false one is the same defect class as a doctor command that reports credentials fine without ever checking them: the promise, not the write, is the harm. The replacement is mcp:local-write, a tier this same engine already defines and already uses for `teach` and `playbook amend`: writes land only in the CLI's own local store, never in external state and never in a user-visible file, so the walker registers destructiveHint=false and openWorldHint=false while leaving readOnlyHint unset. Measured at the live MCP server before and after: recall and playbook_list went from readOnlyHint=true, openWorldHint=true to readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false, openWorldHint=false. AGENTS.md is press-generated and carried the same claim in prose, so the annotation sentence there was regenerated from the booted server's tools/list and is pinned by the AGENTS.md asserts below. This is a TRUTH fix, not a behaviour fix - the RunE bodies are untouched and both commands still write exactly what they wrote before. Upstream closed this wontfix (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so a reprint reintroduces the false annotation and this ledger is the only thing that catches it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Upstream declined (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so there is nothing to encode in the press today. If that is ever revisited, the rule is mechanical rather than a judgement call: a command whose RunE reaches store.OpenWithContext, appendLearningsAudit or any Insert must not carry mcp:read-only. `learnings list`, `learnings candidates` and `learnings stats` are the remaining teach-loop siblings: each still carries mcp:read-only and each still opens the writable store (creating the database file, running migrations and tightening file modes) though none records a row, and all three were left alone deliberately because the ratified decision named only `recall` and `playbook list`. The same shape is not confined to the teach loop: every command that reads this connector's local mirror opens it through the same read-write call, `analytics` included, so what the press should encode is the mechanical rule above rather than a per-command list.

asserts.contains: // playbook list opens the WRITABLE learn store and appends an
which is narrower than it sounds

handfixes.summary: cmd/immybot-mcp/main.go declares `var version = "0.0.0-dev"` and passes it to server.NewMCPServer, so release.yml's `-X main.version=<tag>` stamps the real release into serverInfo.version (issue #322, PR #323)
handfixes.why: Issue #322: the MCP binary reported a hard-coded literal ("0.0.0-dev") in serverInfo.version instead of the release tag. release.yml builds every MCP with `-ldflags "-X main.version=${version}"` (PR #323) and the press template emits `var version = "0.0.0-dev"` for 63 of 67 connectors; this connector's main.go had drifted to a literal in the NewMCPServer call, and the Go linker silently ignores a -X for a symbol that does not exist (build exit 0, no warning), so the stamp could never land. Proven both ways with a real initialize JSON-RPC over stdio: before the fix `go build -ldflags '-X main.version=9.9.9'` still answered the literal; after it answers 9.9.9. A wrong-looking real version (1.0.0 on a v0.1.x release) is worse than 0.0.0-dev because it reads as intentional. code_only because the explanatory comment above the var names the ldflags mechanism; the assert must be satisfied by the declaration itself.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: None needed at the press: current cli-printing-press already emits the var and passes it (see any of the 63 standard mains). A reprint from any current press regenerates this correctly; retire the entry after the next reprint confirms the var is present.

handfixes.summary: The MCP server resolves its config through config.Load("") - honouring IMMYBOT_CONFIG and IMMYBOT_NO_CONFIG_WRITE exactly like the CLI - instead of a hardcoded ~/.config/immybot-cli/config.toml (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270 companion to the fleet's mcp-config-resolves-like-the-cli entries. immybot's MCP server already resolves its config through config.Load("") (newMCPConfig in internal/mcp/tools.go, honouring IMMYBOT_CONFIG and IMMYBOT_NO_CONFIG_WRITE), but it was the one honourer of the switch with no test pinning that resolution, so a reprint from a press whose template hardcodes ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml would silently restore the defect the other 11 honourers are guarded against. The test seeds a config at a non-default path, points IMMYBOT_CONFIG at it, and asserts newMCPConfig returns that file's Path and base_url. The assert on tools.go pins the resolver call itself.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should generate newMCPClient (and the platform-bound newMCPConfig variant) with config.Load("") rather than a hand-built home-relative path; the hardcoded path is a generator defect that makes <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

handfixes.summary: `workflow archive` reports the number of resources that actually succeeded and exits non-zero when 0 of N did; partial success stays exit 0 (issue #275 finding 3, upstream #4410)
handfixes.why: DONE UPSTREAM: mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4410 merged 2026-08-28 (28c43fa9), first shipped press v4.31.3 (2026-08-30). Issue #275 finding 3 (@Xenith-B): `workflow archive` reported `"resources_synced": len(resources)` and returned nil even when every resource errored or warned, so the JSON summary and the human line (`Archived 0 items across N resources`) were success-shaped for a tenant whose every request 401ed, and an agent reading them believed the archive was complete. immybot's 4.3x-era print already counted resourcesSynced and reported it, but never errored on zero, so an all-failed archive still exited 0 with a success-shaped human line; only the zero-guard and the summary suppression from the upstream template diff were added. The three outcomes are pinned by workflow_archive_outcome_test.go, which drives the real root command against a local HTTP double with dummy credentials: every resource 401 -> non-zero exit naming `0 of N resource(s) archived`, resources_synced 0, and no success-shaped summary; one resource serving rows and the rest 401 -> exit 0 with resources_synced 1 (the TRUE count) and the per-resource errors on stderr; every resource serving an empty page -> exit 0 with every attempted resource counted. Partial success stays exit 0, matching sync's default non-strict policy. This connector is on press an unstamped 4.3x-era print, below the first fixed release, so a reprint from the vendored engine REINTRODUCES the false success while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices. Retire it after a reprint from press >= 4.31.3.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: None: the fix is in the press template since 4.31.3. A reprint from >= 4.31.3 regenerates it; keep the behavioural test, which is a hand-authored (NOVEL) file regen-merge preserves.

asserts.contains: return fmt.Errorf("workflow archive failed: 0 of %d resource(s) archived", len(resources))

handfixes.summary: MCP discovery exposes executor-facing request schemas and indexes input names and known enum values
handfixes.why: Issue #351: endpoint summaries omitted required request inputs. Keep canonical JSON body case and nesting, path/header/query routing, and exact short request search terms. Contracts are derived from the shipped CLI source, and the existing CLI commands and auth remain intact. Upstream request metadata fix #4890 was not merged when this surgical repair was made.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Replace this downstream contract extraction only when a released Printing Press generates equally complete executor-facing schemas and preserves every existing hand-fix.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 12 commands listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs them
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: access create-delete-azure-tenant-auth-details (POST /api/v1/auth/delete-azure-tenant-auth-details); application-locks create-request-cancellation (POST /api/v1/application-locks/request-cancellation); billing create-cancel-subscription (POST /api/v1/billing/cancel-subscription); computers ephemeral-agent-circuit-breaker create-reset (POST /api/v1/computers/{computerId}/ephemeral-agent-circuit-breaker/reset); maintenance-sessions actions create-by-id-rerun (POST /api/v1/maintenance-sessions/{sessionId}/actions/{actionId}/rerun); maintenance-sessions create-cancel (POST /api/v1/maintenance-sessions/cancel); metrics create-circuit-breakers-isolate (POST /api/v1/metrics/circuit-breakers/isolate); plugins create-api-v1-by-provider-link-id-by-catch-all (POST /plugins/api/v1/{providerLinkId}/{catchAll}); provider-agents create-bulk-delete-pending (POST /api/v1/provider-agents/bulk-delete-pending); provider-links cross-references create-by-external-link-id-disable-client-linking (POST /api/v1/provider-links/{id}/cross-references/{externalLinkId}/disable-client-linking); scripts create-debug-cancel-by-cancellation-id (POST /api/v1/scripts/debug/cancel/{cancellationId}); system create-disable-immy-support-access (POST /api/v1/system/disable-immy-support-access).

handfixes.summary: --dry-run never mints a token or changes stored credentials: neither the client's automatic client-credentials mint nor `auth login --dry-run` sends the client secret to the token URL, and `auth set-token --dry-run` and `auth logout --dry-run` neither save nor clear anything

handfixes.summary: Every token request (auth login, the automatic client-credentials mint and the refresh grant) goes through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient, which follows same-origin redirects only, so the client secret never reaches a host a redirect from the token URL names
handfixes.why: Owner decision on PR #441 (finish the auth-wire class). `auth login` (through http.DefaultClient) and the automatic client-credentials mint and refresh grant (through c.HTTPClient, whose CheckRedirect follows a 307 to another host) replayed the token request body, the client secret included, to whatever host a redirect from the token URL named. Printed before press 4.33.5, which routes every token request through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient (a token client that follows same-origin hops only); this back-ports that file verbatim and uses it at the same call sites. TestAuthLoginRefusesATokenRedirectToAnotherOrigin and TestTokenMintRefusesARedirectToAnotherOrigin failed on the previous commit (the second host received the token request) and pass now. The host compare is also hardened (see the newer-print entries): an IP literal compares exactly, IPv6 zone included; a DNS name folds ASCII case only.

handfixes.summary: the vendor swagger is repaired before generation so the 4.34.0 print keeps the shipped command names, body flags and per-instance server
handfixes.why: The swagger (an instance's own /swagger/v1/swagger.json, vendored by BezaluLLC/Bezalu.ImmyBot.Client) has no operationIds, no servers and no security. Without operationIds 4.34.0 names opId-less operations list/get/create plus a collision suffix, which would rename 429 of 735 shipped commands and break every script, SKILL reference, MCP endpoint id and request-contract key; the spec builder pins each operationId to the shipped endpoint name. Swashbuckle marks get-only C# collections the server binds as readOnly, and 4.34.0 drops readOnly body fields, which removed 38 shipped flags (--computer-ids, --agent-ids, --parameters, ...); the builder strips readOnly from request-reachable schemas only. providerLinkExternalReferenceData stays one opaque JSON flag because 4.34.0 flattens it into an MCP key over the 64-character limit. The server is https://{subdomain}.immy.bot with IMMYBOT_SUBDOMAIN, auth is Entra client credentials, and /api/v1/auth/* is the access resource so it does not collide with the framework auth command. The PM archetype (stale, orphans, load) ties with content on keyword score and Go map order picks, so a reprint must re-render until root.go registers newStaleCmd.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Encoded in the spec by the factory's build_spec.py, so it survives a reprint by construction once that script runs on any new swagger. Press items: deterministic archetype tie-break; readOnly handling that keeps request properties the server binds.

handfixes.summary: the derived OAuth scope reads IMMYBOT_BASE_URL and IMMYBOT_SUBDOMAIN through cliutil.EnvOverride, so a blank .mcpb field never becomes the scope
handfixes.why: A Claude Desktop .mcpb install passes an unfilled optional field as the literal string ${user_config.immybot_base_url}. The shipped scope hook read the variables raw with os.Getenv, so that unresolved placeholder became the OAuth scope and Entra rejected every token request. config.Load already ignores unresolved placeholders through cliutil.EnvOverride; the scope hook now resolves the same way.

handfixes.summary: the mirror-reading commands open the local store read-only and key fleet-diff snapshots at nanosecond precision

They now open it through immyOpenMirror (read-only); only fleet-diff --snapshot opens it writable. A missing table reads as not synced (immyNoSuchTable) instead of an error. Snapshot keys carry nanoseconds so two snapshots in the same second never collide.

One credkit.Declarations literal in internal/credwire/declarations.go names every credential source and where each may go; credkit.Start is the first statement of both mains and credkit.Exit the last; stdout and stderr, every file write, every SQLite handle, MCP stdio and HTTP, every outbound client and child processes pass the kit. The credential store and the config file are declared sources and are written outside the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile). Every source is held right after Start, before any argument is parsed (the kit: URLEnv, proxies; credwire.HoldStartup: every value of every file a run could read), and a request's declared credential fields as soon as its body exists, before any --dry-run preview (credwire.HoldRequest); a profile's credential flag values when the store is read (credwire.HoldProfileValues). The run profile store is a source held right after Start through an allow-list (internal/cli/immybot_profile_hold.go), not one of the kit's Files, which would hold its own JSON keys. handfixes.why: assignment-explain, computer-dossier, psa-reconcile and fleet-diff read name/tenant/online from computers-paged rows, whose ComputerListViewModel fields are computerName/tenantName/isOnline, so a paged computer was not found and its changes were invisible; version-spread counted every machine with a title as behind; session-triage counted computers and tenants by name. Every roster read now goes through the merged immyLoadComputers record, and a source-scan test refuses a command that selects roster rows itself. The merged record then let the first source that carried a value win, so a later sync of one source (sync --resources computers-paged saying isOnline:false) could not replace an older value another source left, in fleet-diff and computer-dossier alike. Each field now comes from the newest-synced row that carries it (a null still never hides a value), and the fleet-diff fingerprint also carries every source value that disagrees with the merged record, so a change in any one source is a change even when two syncs land in the same second. Rows now join a computer by computer id only (immyComputerJoinFor binds the id alone), a Computer rule reaches its computer by id only, and computer-dossier counts the rows with no computer id in unidentified_actions and unidentified_software. A source-scan test refuses a SQL comparison of a mirrored computer name or a join built from a shape's name field.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored, sync keeps walking, and the run still succeeds, naming the row ids on stderr and in its summary
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows). synccpu (2026-11-09): a withheld row no longer fails the resource. mcp2 measured hubspot-calls-crm row 80663490159 turning the whole sync into exit 1, so the server never marked the connector synced. Now the resource ends stored with the ids named (stderr warning, a sync_warning rows_withheld event per page, and "withheld" in the summary), the run exits 0 when every other row stored, and the resource's checkpoint stays where the attempt began so the next run fetches the row again.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).

handfixes.summary: The <api>_search tool's description ends with the API's resource families (codeOrchSearchResources in internal/mcp/search_desc.go, from codeOrchEndpoints, capped at 300 characters).
handfixes.why: The generated description was the same in every connector and named no resource, so a host that ranks tools by words put other tools above <api>_search for "<api> <resource>" (#629; zammad_search ranked 13th of 45 for "zammad tickets"). A reprint regenerates code_orch.go without the call; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json mcp-search-desc-resources).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (upstream PR named in fleet_handfixes.json): the code-orchestration template should build the <api>_search description from the endpoint registry's resource families.

handfixes.summary: Both client-credentials mints (the client's automatic mint and auth login) send client_id and client_secret in the form body with grant_type first, never as HTTP Basic, so a renewal is not withheld as a piece of the token it replaces
handfixes.why: Issue #698, the same class as nerdio's #691. The first Entra token is held as a credential that may go only to the ImmyBot instance. The renewal sent the client pair as HTTP Basic, and the credential kit withheld that request as carrying a piece of the held token (an Entra token's payload carries the client ID), so the server worked until its first token expired and could never mint again until restart, and the first mint after a restart that loaded an expired token from the config file was withheld the same way. In the form body the client ID is plain text, so the request no longer carries what the token does. Exempting minted tokens at the token endpoint was rejected: it widens where a token may go. grant_type must stay first (cliutil.TokenForm): the kit reads a form body as one key=value line, and url.Values.Encode sorts client_id first. Entra accepts both forms. TestRenewalMintIsNotWithheld drives the real kit and client at each base64 alignment of the client ID inside the token, for a renewal and for a restart; on the Basic code the aligned shape fails both with the withhold notice. The kit fleet test TestKitFleetBasicMintRenewalIsNotWithheld (tools/maintainer/credkit) fails if a reprint brings the Basic mint back. A reprint restores SetBasicAuth. The unused refreshAccessToken is left as generated: nothing calls it. Spec-encode candidate: the press should offer form-body client authentication for an OAuth2 token endpoint on another origin.
